subproblem.title: A positive multiple of an oriented n-plane with the integer slice property has integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Hypothesis names: (REP), (MR), (SL) are the exact frozen statements of the DAG theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_slice_mass_bounds (hypotheses of the selected parent cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity); (RU) is the exact frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, (CT) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) that of cbr_measure_convergence_tools, (RECT) that of cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent; whichever are needed appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement. In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Radon μ (against C_c, limsup on compacts ≤ μ, liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; (MM) if Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) on (a, b) then some measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) has ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors, admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P: μ Borel, finite on compact sets, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. ISP (integer slice property) of Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity. Assume (MR) and (SL). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, v = (v_1, …, v_n) orthonormal in ℝ^P, V₀ := span(v), θ₀ > 0 and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with C(ω) = θ₀∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v_1, …, v_n)dHⁿ(y) for every test form ω. If C has ISP, then θ₀ is a natural number.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 10 (V14, integrality), using the sibling const_mass (cm) for the mass formula of step 5(δ) in degree n − 1. Fact (O) (orthogonal invariance of the coefficient norm; proved here because the accepted DAG lemmas regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis / regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le / regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one are not prerequisites of this node). For an orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_P) of ℝ^P and a k-covector α, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)})² = k!·|α|²: the left side is the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear map α and does not depend on the orthonormal basis (expand α(Of_{j(1)}, …) multilinearly and use Σ_l O_{la}O_{lb} = δ_{ab}); for the standard basis non-injective j contribute 0 and each increasing multi-index I contributes k! equal terms α(e_I)². Consequences: (O1) if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²); (O2) β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector (multilinear and alternating in u) with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k)); (O3) if p : ℝ^P → ℝ^k, p(x) = (⟨x, v_1⟩, …, ⟨x, v_k⟩) with v orthonormal, then the pulled-back covector p^#γ := γ∘(p × ⋯ × p) of an l-covector γ on ℝ^k has |p^#γ| = |γ| (in a basis f extending v, p(f_i) = e_i for i ≤ k and 0 otherwise). 
0. Coordinates. Let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ι(z) := Σ_jz_jv_j, a linear isometry onto V₀; Hⁿ⌞V₀ = ι_*(Lⁿ) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). For a test k-form ω on ℝ^P let ω̃ := ι^#ω, ω̃(z)(u) := ω(ιz)(ιu_1, …, ιu_k), smooth with compact support on ℝⁿ (ι is proper). Then C(ω) = θ₀∫_{ℝⁿ}ω(ιz)(v)dz = θ₀∫_{ℝⁿ}ω̃(z)(e_1, …, e_n)dz, and d commutes with ι^#. Let f(y) := ⟨y, v_1⟩ (1-Lipschitz).
1. ∂C = 0. For a test d-form φ on ℝ^P, with φ̃_j(z) := φ̃(z)(e_1, …, ê_j, …, e_n) ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ): ∂C(φ) = C(dφ) = θ₀∫_{ℝⁿ}(dφ̃)(z)(e_1, …, e_n)dz = θ₀Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}∫_{ℝⁿ}∂_jφ̃_j dz = 0 (exteriorDerivative_apply; the integral of a partial derivative of a compactly supported C¹ function vanishes by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus). For n = 1: ∂C(φ) = θ₀∫_ℝ(φ∘ι)'(z)dz = 0.
2. Slices. (μ, ξ) := (θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, ξ_v), ξ_v(β) := β(v), is an admissible representation of C: μ is finite on compacts, ξ_v is constant with |ξ_v(β)| ≤ |β| (O1), and C(ω) = ∫ξ_v(ω)dμ. (0, 0) represents ∂C = 0. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, this data, f, L := 1: currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ_v(ω)dμ = θ₀∫_{V₀∩{f<t}}ω(v)dHⁿ and B_t(φ) = 0. ISP of C instantiated with (μ, ξ_v), (0, 0) and f gives an L¹-null set N such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity for every t ∉ N; Z_t(φ) = ∂A_t(φ).
3. Z_t by the divergence theorem on a half-space. V₀ ∩ {f < t} = ι({z_1 < t}). For a test d-form φ, Z_t(φ) = A_t(dφ) = θ₀∫_{z_1<t}Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}∂_jφ̃_j dz. For j ≥ 2, integrating first in z_j over ℝ gives 0; for j = 1, ∫_{z_1<t}∂_1φ̃_1dz = ∫_{ℝ^{n−1}}φ̃_1(t, z')dz'. Hence Z_t(φ) = θ₀∫_{ℝ^{n−1}}φ(ι(t, z'))(v_2, …, v_n)dz' = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(v_2, …, v_n)dH^d(y), where L_t := V₀ ∩ {f = t} = ι({t} × ℝ^{n−1}) and H^d⌞L_t is the image of L^{n−1} under the isometry z' ↦ ι(t, z'). For n = 1, Z_t(φ) = θ₀φ(tv_1) = θ₀∫φ dH⁰⌞{tv_1} (μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero). In all cases Z_t(φ) = ∫ζ₁(φ(y))dν'(y) with ν' := H^d⌞L_t (finite on compacts) and the constant d-vector ζ₁(γ) := θ₀γ(v_2, …, v_n) (γ ↦ θ₀γ() for d = 0).
4. Mass of Z_t. (v_2, …, v_n) is orthonormal, so |ζ₁(γ)| ≤ θ₀|γ| (O1), and γ₁ := β_{(v_2,…,v_n)} (γ₁ := 1 if d = 0) has |γ₁| = 1 and ζ₁(γ₁) = θ₀ (O2). By (cm) with m := d, ζ₀ := ζ₁, s := θ₀: M_G(Z_t) = θ₀H^d(L_t ∩ G) for every open G.
5. Comparison with an IMRep. Fix t ∉ N and an IMRep R = (M_t, θ', ξ') of Z_t. By (MR), M_G(Z_t) = R.measure(G) = ∫⁻_{M_t∩G}θ'dH^d for every open G. So the Borel measures R.measure and θ₀H^d⌞L_t agree on all open sets; both are finite on the balls B_j(0) (θ₀H^d(L_t ∩ B_j(0)) < ∞, and R.measure(B_j(0)) = M_{B_j(0)}(Z_t) equals it); open sets form a π-system generating the Borel sets, so R.measure = θ₀H^d⌞L_t (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion).
6. Integrality. D := L_t ∩ B_1(tv_1) is Borel with 0 < H^d(D) < ∞ (a d-dimensional unit ball in L_t; for d = 0, D = {tv_1} and H⁰(D) = 1). By step 5, θ₀H^d(D∖M_t) = R.measure(D∖M_t) = 0, so H^d(D∖M_t) = 0 and H^d(D ∩ M_t) = H^d(D) > 0. For Borel E ⊆ D ∩ M_t, ∫⁻_Eθ'dH^d = R.measure(E) = θ₀H^d(E); hence θ' = θ₀ H^d-a.e. on D ∩ M_t (ae_eq_of_forall_setLIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite), and since H^d(D ∩ M_t) > 0 there is x ∈ D ∩ M_t with θ'(x) = θ₀. θ' takes values in ℕ, so θ₀ = θ'(x) ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂C = 0 and (θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, v∧) is an admissible representation; (SL) and ISP of C make Z_t = ∂(C⌞{⟨·,v_1⟩ < t}) IM for a.e. t.
Divergence theorem on a half-space: Z_t(φ) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(v_2, …, v_n)dH^d.
(cm) gives M_G(Z_t) = θ₀H^d(L_t ∩ G); (MR) gives M_G(Z_t) = R.measure(G) for an IMRep R of Z_t.
R.measure = θ₀H^d⌞L_t forces the integer multiplicity θ' to equal θ₀ on a set of positive measure, so θ₀ ∈ ℕ.

audit.reason: The half-space boundary computation, ISP, const_mass and MR identify a positive constant density with an IMRep multiplicity on a set of positive finite measure. This proves the natural-number conclusion, including d = 0.
